name: Adrenal fatigue protocols

card.summary: Supplement-and-lifestyle routines aimed at supposedly worn-out adrenal glands, used by people hoping to restore energy, recovery and training capacity that show up as a fuller, fitter physique.
card.aka: Adrenal support protocols, adrenal reset, cortisol cocktail
card.note: Adrenal fatigue is not a recognised medical diagnosis; unneeded adrenal hormone products can suppress the adrenal glands.

quick.overview:
Adrenal fatigue is an alternative-medicine term for adrenal glands said to be exhausted by chronic stress, leaving a person tired, sleeping badly and slow to recover. Protocols built around it are meant to restore energy and training capacity, which people connect to better gym performance, leaner body composition and a healthier-looking face.

The idea was coined in 1998 by chiropractor James Wilson. The Endocrine Society states there is no scientific proof that it is a real medical condition, and a 2016 systematic review found no support for it. Within lifting and TRT communities, however, the concept is widely discussed as an explanation for burnout after stimulant use or hormone therapy.
quick.how: In practice people combine stress reduction and sleep changes with over-the-counter adrenal support supplements, herbal adaptogens, DHEA or pregnenolone, and sometimes glandular products, often guided by saliva or blood cortisol tests or by a naturopath. Some also cut back on caffeine and stimulant pre-workouts. Forum users describe these routines as lasting weeks to months.
quick.risks: The Endocrine Society warns that adrenal supplements are not FDA-approved or tested for safety, may not match their labels, and that taking adrenal hormones that are not needed can suppress the glands and potentially lead to adrenal crisis. Persistent fatigue can also reflect real conditions such as adrenal insufficiency, depression or sleep apnea, which the Society says deserve proper evaluation.

lead: Adrenal fatigue is a term from alternative medicine for adrenal glands that are said to become exhausted by prolonged stress and so under-produce cortisol and related hormones [1]. Protocols built around it combine supplements, diet and stress management and are aimed at relieving tiredness, poor sleep and slow recovery [1].

In looksmaxxing and bodybuilding circles the appeal is the chain from energy to appearance: if recovery and drive improve, people can train harder and more consistently, which supports muscle, leanness and overall presentation. The term appears on T Nation forum threads about stimulant overuse, testosterone replacement, thyroid and DHEA, where users describe adrenal support as one more lever [2][3][4].

The term was coined in 1998 by chiropractor James Wilson [1]. The Endocrine Society states that there is no scientific proof it is a real medical condition and that no valid test exists for it [5]; a 2016 systematic review likewise found no evidence supporting it [1].

angle.text: Followers use adrenal protocols hoping to feel less drained so they can train, sleep and recover better, which they link to a stronger physique and healthier appearance. The route to looks is indirect and runs through energy and training capacity.

paras: Proponents describe adrenal fatigue as a state in which the adrenal glands, worn down by chronic stress or illness, cannot keep up with demand for cortisol and other hormones. Reported symptoms are nonspecific: tiredness, trouble sleeping, cravings and low motivation [1][5]. It is separate from adrenal insufficiency and Addison's disease, which are diagnosed endocrine disorders [1].

Chiropractor James Wilson introduced the term in 1998 [1]. A supplement industry developed around it, offering adrenal support formulas and testing [1]. In 2023 a social-media trend called the cortisol cocktail, a mix of fruit juice, coconut water and salt, was popularised in this space [1].

On T Nation, users in testosterone replacement, stimulant and thyroid threads mention adrenal fatigue as a cause of exhaustion after heavy stimulant use or hormone adjustments, and ask coaches about products to counter it [2][4]. One coach-Q&A questioner reports leaning on stimulants for a long time and asks which protocol would address adrenal fatigue [8].

Typical routines described by forum users include working with a naturopath on diet and supplementation, adding DHEA and adrenal support complexes, bovine adrenal products, and cutting back on stimulants [3][6]. Some users combine this with thyroid and testosterone management, and others in the same communities caution that chasing many parameters at once can add to stress [7].
A 2016 systematic review found no evidence supporting adrenal fatigue as a condition [1]. No clinical trial has tested a branded adrenal fatigue protocol for appearance outcomes.

The Endocrine Society says no test can detect adrenal fatigue, that the symptoms overlap with adrenal insufficiency, depression and obstructive sleep apnea, and that those possibilities should be evaluated [5]. It warns that adrenal supplements are not FDA-approved or tested for safety and may differ from their labels, and that taking adrenal hormones unnecessarily can stop the glands working, potentially causing life-threatening adrenal crisis [5]. Mayo Clinic is cited as stating it is not an accepted diagnosis [1].

timeline.event: James Wilson coins the term adrenal fatigue [1].
A systematic review finds no evidence for the condition [1].
The cortisol cocktail spreads on social media [1].

lore.intro: Adrenal fatigue comes up in T Nation threads on stimulant burnout, TRT and thyroid self-management [2][3][4].

claims.claim: Long stimulant use leaves the adrenals exhausted
claims.believers: Users who relied on pre-workout stimulants describe crashing and ask for products to counter adrenal fatigue [8].
claims.experts: The Endocrine Society says there is no scientific proof adrenal fatigue is a real condition and that symptoms such as tiredness have many other possible causes [5].

claims.claim: DHEA and adrenal support complexes restore low cortisol and DHEA
claims.believers: Forum posters recommend adding DHEA and adrenal support complexes to a TRT recovery routine [3].
claims.experts: The Endocrine Society warns that unneeded adrenal hormones can suppress adrenal function and risk adrenal crisis [5].

claims.claim: Naturopathic adrenal healing resolves fatigue on TRT
claims.believers: One user reports working with a naturopath who attributed his insomnia to adrenal fatigue and treated it with supplements and diet [2].
claims.experts: No published trial supports adrenal fatigue treatment; a 2016 review found no evidence for the condition [1].
